summary:
Set 120 Session 1 makes the activity-log step-status field a closed vocabulary and the writer strict about it, after measuring that roughly 10% of the step entries on disk carry a token no reader can name.

(1) THE MEASUREMENT WAS REPRODUCED, NOT INHERITED. The spec's counts came from a one-off query; this session re-ran the count over every activity-log.json before drawing anything from it. Confirmed canonical: complete 2,417 / pending 55 / in-progress 31 / blocked 3. The drift totals moved slightly against the spec (complete 2,417 vs 2,412, pending 55 vs 45, nine prose blobs vs '~6') because Set 119 kept writing after the spec was authored and this session's own registration seeded five plan rows. This is reported, not silently met; Session 2 is spec-mandated to reconcile the exact numbers and say whether a discrepancy is about the query or about the spec.

(2) THE VOCABULARY IS THE INTERSECTION OF MEASURED AND NAMEABLE -- WHICH IS WHY IT IS FOUR TOKENS, NOT FIVE. The first cut took the spec's five candidates on the strength of the counts alone. Round 1 discovery found, on BOTH lenses independently, that 'skipped' was legal at the writer but nameable by no reader: no entry in session_checklist.STATUS_BOXES (so it renders '[?]', the corrupt-data glyph) and not terminal in _mark_here or the Work Explorer's mirrored markHere (so a skipped step steals the '<- here' marker from real work). That is Set 119 S2's failure with a different token -- the session's own deliverable reproducing the defect it exists to close. FREQUENCY ON DISK IS NOT THE TEST FOR ADMISSION TO A WRITER VOCABULARY; NAMEABILITY BY EVERY READER IS. The legal set is complete / in-progress / pending / blocked.

(3) THE WRITER FAILS CLOSED, AND EVERY SIBLING WRITER ROUTES THROUGH THE SAME CHOKEPOINT. require_step_status raises InvalidStepStatusError (a ValueError subclass, mirroring Set 086 S1's InvalidVerificationVerdictError) BEFORE the entry is appended, so a refused write leaves the log byte-identical. Four modules bypass SessionLog with their own read-modify-write of activity-log.json -- contract_gate, path_aware_critique, dual_surface_verify, suggestion_disposition. All four already hard-coded 'complete', so none could drift at runtime today, but an allowlist at one entry point is worthless if another path writes the file directly (L-069-1). Each now spells the token from the shared STEP_STATUS_COMPLETE constant and passes it through the chokepoint, and a structural ast scan over every production module enforces the rule for a writer nobody has written yet.

(4) THE FALSIFIERS ACTUALLY FALSIFY, PROVEN BY MUTATION. 22 test functions / 55 cases plant every measured drifted token (completed, done, complete-with-known-failures, skipped, prose, None, empty, near-miss casing) through the PUBLIC entrypoint and assert refusal with a message naming the legal set, alongside positives asserting every canonical token still lands and the pending -> in-progress -> complete lifecycle survives. With the two require_step_status guards replaced by 'pass', 34 of the cases fail -- the guards are load-bearing, not decorative. Per L-112-1 the ast guard carries its own planted-violation falsifier AND a session-state look-alike negative, since a scan that matches nothing looks identical to one that finds nothing.

(5) READERS WERE NOT TOUCHED, AND A TEST ASSERTS IT. Standing decision 1 holds: history on disk stays readable, STATUS_BOXES still renders 'done' as [x] and 'completed' as [?], and a 1,000-character prose status still does not crash the renderer.

Verification: three rounds. Discovery (2-lens fan-out) found the 'skipped' defect on both lenses; supplementary found one Major that was DISMISSED as out-of-scope (a concurrent extension session's uncommitted work leaked into the evidence bundle via the working-tree diff); remediation-review returned VERIFIED with 2 fix-accepted and zero findings. Cross-provider to gpt-5.5 with anthropic excluded throughout.

reason.specifics: Session 2 inherits an unusually well-specified job -- inventory the ~281 drifted entries precisely, present the three-option ruling to the operator, and execute it idempotently -- and its main risk is not reasoning difficulty but discipline: it rewrites historical records, and the spec requires it to state whether any discrepancy with this spec's counts is a fact about the query or about the spec. Continuity matters more than a fresh lens here, because this session already re-ran the counts, already found where the drift concentrates (completed in 18 sets, done in 5, eight of nine prose blobs in Set 110 and the ninth in Set 068), and already established that the single 'skipped' entry is a session-level skip logged as a step. Cross-provider independence is preserved where it counts: session-verification continues to route away from anthropic.

notes.session_position: Session 1 of 3, NOT set-terminal. No change-log.md is authored here (it belongs to Session 3), and `pathAwareCritique` is deliberately absent from this set's configuration, so no critique artifact is owed at any point in the set. Nothing is published: the package stays at 1.0.0 and the Set 120 changelog section is [Unreleased].
notes.the_finding_that_changed_the_deliverable: Round 1's finding is the most important thing in this session. Both discovery lenses -- spec-conformance and failure-scenario, run independently over the same evidence -- reported the same defect: 'skipped' was accepted by the new writer but rendered [?] by the reader and treated as non-terminal by both the CLI and the Explorer, so a skipped step would steal the current-step marker. My step 2 obeyed the spec's letter ('confirm against the counts above; do not invent') and stopped at frequency. The correct admission test is nameability by every reader, and the vocabulary is now the intersection of the two. The fix narrowed the writer rather than widening a reader, which satisfies the acceptance criterion's GOAL (no accepted token is unrenderable) more completely than teaching one of two readers would have.
operator_decisions: Exclude 'skipped' from the vocabulary (authority=human, rubric_line=escalate-to-human, verification_effect=strengthens, reversible). Escalated rather than self-decided because the choice traded expressiveness against an EXTERNAL constraint -- a concurrent extension session editing tools/ in the same checkout -- and because narrowing contradicted the spec's letter while serving its goal. The three rejected alternatives (teach both readers; teach Python only; Python box only) and their consequences are recorded in decisions.jsonl and argued in s1-remediation-round-1.md. 'skipped' can return when both readers can name it, which happens naturally with the extension carve.
notes.verification_loop: THREE rounds, all cross-provider to gpt-5.5 with the orchestrator's effective provider (anthropic, via model-registry lookup on claude-opus-5) excluded. Round 1 `--phase discovery`, 2-call fan-out: 2 blocking, both lenses independently finding the 'skipped' defect. Round 2 `--phase supplementary` run BEFORE any remediation, as the loop discipline requires: 1 blocking, dismissed (see contaminated_evidence below). Round 3 `--phase remediation-review` over the fix delta: VERIFIED, 2 fix-accepted, 0 rejected, 0 accepted-with-modification, 0 findings. No finding was disputed on its merits, so nothing was waived and there is no adjudicated-minor residual. The acceptance harness ran for both findings-bearing rounds; all three findings were judgment-kind, so none auto-closed by baseline discrimination and all were settled by the review round. Cost recorded as $0.00: this is a Copilot CLI seat, where billed usage is unavailable by design. An up-front conventions block (s1-conventions.md) carried the suite baseline, the release contract, six by-design exclusions and the consequence rubric per L-064-10, and was updated between rounds so the review round was told what had changed and why.
notes.contaminated_evidence: Round 2's Major finding described a broken extension copy-prompt surface and a failing `tsc` in tools/. It was accurate about the TREE and wrong about ATTRIBUTION, and the attribution error was mine to prevent. verify_session assembles evidence from `git status --short` plus the complete WORKING-TREE diff, and the operator was concurrently editing the Work Explorer in a separate chat session with that work uncommitted, so it was handed to the verifier as part of this session's change set. `git diff --cached --name-only -- tools/` was empty and this session never opened a file under tools/. Dismissed as out-of-scope with operator confirmation, per the workflow's adjudication path; the tsc failure it surfaced was relayed to the extension session as live feedback and was genuinely useful. The concurrent work was then stashed for the remainder of this session, and round 3 ran over a tree containing only this session's work.
notes.process_defect_for_step_9: Two sessions in one checkout is a hazard the framework does not currently name. Beyond the evidence contamination above, verification_stamp.compute_work_diff_sha256 digests every file differing from base under only dist/out/node_modules/.venv/__pycache__/*.vsix -- so tools/**/src/** and package.json BIND an ai_router session's freshness stamp. A concurrent editor's saves therefore stale a verification they have nothing to do with, which can fire the close backstop and spend a metered round to re-stamp a tree whose own work is byte-identical. `--exclude` narrows the evidence bundle but NOT the digest, so it is only half a mitigation. The parallel-worktree layout in docs/planning/repo-worktree-layout.md exists precisely to keep two sessions out of one checkout and was not used. Carried to Step 9 as a candidate lesson; Session 3 of this set is the natural place to act on it if it is judged in scope.
notes.test_run_of_record: pytest is the only expensive suite this session owes: run_of_record's `covers` puts ai_router/ under pytest, while playwright covers tools/** plus session_state.py / start_session.py / close_session.py -- none of which this session touched. That is consistent with the spec's requiresE2E: false, and it is a measured claim rather than an appeal to the flag. The run was made on the frozen tree AFTER the last code change and recorded in test-runs.jsonl.
notes.irony_budget: The set caps new test functions at 40 across all three sessions. This session shipped 22 (55 parametrised cases) in one module, ai_router/tests/test_step_status_vocabulary.py, leaving 18 for Sessions 2 and 3. Three of the 22 were added during remediation and are the ones that matter most: test_every_accepted_token_is_renderable_by_the_reader is the invariant whose absence caused round 1's finding, and it fails if the writer is ever widened without teaching the reader.
owed_residuals: The ~281 drifted entries already on disk are untouched. Session 2 owns the inventory, the operator ruling and any migration; 'history still contains completed' is the expected end state of THIS session, not a defect in it.

Absence is still allowed through append_entry. A status-less bookkeeping entry is accepted, because 'no status recorded' is a different defect from 'a status no reader can name', and Session 3 owns it explicitly (unknown / stale / unreadable). Four such entries exist on disk, all in Set 028. If Session 3 wants absence refused at the writer too, that is a vocabulary decision to make on purpose, not a gap to patch quietly.

session_checklist.seed_plan_steps wraps its append_entry loop in `except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, ImportError): return []`, and InvalidStepStatusError is a ValueError -- so a fail-closed writer sits behind a fail-open caller. There is no runtime path to a silent failure today because the seeded status is a module constant that the vocabulary test locks, but a future change making it dynamic would fail open. Named so it is a decision, not an oversight.

'skipped' has no canonical spelling until both readers learn it. Callers are directed to the step description by the refusal message. The two-language fix (STATUS_BOXES + _mark_here in Python, TERMINAL_STATUSES + STATUS_GLYPHS in sessionStepModel.ts, plus a parity corpus case) belongs with the extension carve.

The parity corpus has no case exercising any token outside {complete, done, pending, in-progress}. It would not have caught a Python-only terminal-set change, which is why that option was rejected rather than merely disliked.
notes.next_session_note: Session 2 should run its drift inventory from a COMMAND, as its spec requires, and compare against this session's reproduced figures rather than the spec's: complete 2,417 / completed 229 / pending 55 / done 42 / in-progress 31 / None 4 / blocked 3 / skipped 1 / complete-with-known-failures 1 / nine prose blobs. Note that this session's own writes have since added canonical entries, so the numbers will have moved again -- which is precisely why the spec asks for a command and not a constant.
